claims.statement: validateOkfFrontmatter parses the leading `---` block and returns structured issues (each with a stable code, optional line, and message) rather than throwing, so callers get machine-readable validation results.

`type` is the only required OKF frontmatter field; its absence produces a `missing_type` validation issue, while `title`, `description`, `resource`, and the tolerated legacy `timestamp` are only checked to be non-empty strings when present.
When present, `tags` must be a YAML list of non-empty strings or validation reports `invalid_tags`.

validateOkfFrontmatter validates the OKF v0.2 provenance/trust/lifecycle families when present: `generated` as a `{by, at}` actor event, `verified` as one such event or a list of them, `sources` as a list of mappings each with a non-empty `resource`, `status` as one of draft/stable/deprecated, and `stale_after` as an ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit offset.

OKF timestamp-valued fields require an explicit UTC offset and are validated against real calendar components (not just a regex shape) so freshness comparisons never depend on a consumer's local timezone.

normalizeConceptContent delegates to repairOkfFrontmatter, which leaves a page byte-for-byte unchanged when its frontmatter parses and validates. For parseable-but-invalid YAML it edits only the offending recognized field through line-preserving setters; for unparseable or still-invalid YAML it falls back to a minimal block (type, title, and `openwiki_generated: true` via OPENWIKI_GENERATED_FIELD) emitted by renderFrontmatter.

deriveMinimalFrontmatter supplies only a `type` (defaulting to the localized "Reference") and a `title` taken from the first H1 or the filename, deliberately omitting `description` because a code-guessed description is usually poor.

repairOkfFrontmatter preserves producer extension fields (such as openwiki_translation_pending) and valid provenance families byte-for-byte during the surgical repair path, because only recognized invalid fields are touched through line-preserving setters; the minimal-rebuild fallback (unparseable or unrepairable YAML) discards all frontmatter except derived type/title plus the openwiki_generated marker, so extensions and prior provenance are lost only in that last-resort case.

Frontmatter writers edit the raw block line-by-line (setFrontmatterField, setGeneratedEvent, setOkfSources, setOkfVerified, removeFrontmatterField) rather than parsing and re-rendering, preserving every unrelated line byte-for-byte so producer-authored extensions are never dropped; replaceFrontmatterFieldBlock locates one top-level field plus its indented continuation lines and splices only that span.

snapshotGeneratedProvenance records, before authoring, a SHA-256 hash of each concept's exact Markdown body (frontmatter excluded, whitespace retained) plus the prior valid `generated` event, and serializes it in deterministic sorted order so it survives a process restart between phases.

finalizeGeneratedProvenance stamps the run's `generated` event on new pages and any page whose body hash changed (removing the legacy `timestamp`), restores the prior event on unchanged bodies without advancing its timestamp, leaves previously-unstamped unchanged pages unstamped, and refuses to run with an empty producer actor.

synchronizeWikiIndexes renders a deterministic index.md for every directory, listing concept files (link label from the page `title` falling back to the basename, caption from its `description`) and subdirectories, excluding index.md/log.md/INSTRUCTIONS.md and hidden entries.

An index is written only when its rendered content differs from the existing file, so unchanged indexes produce no diff noise; index synchronization also normalizes each concept file it visits so it can read clean metadata.
Only the root directory's index carries an `okf_version: "0.2"` frontmatter marker; nested directory indexes have no frontmatter.

Index section headings and the derived concept `type` word are curated per-language structural chrome: resolveIndexLabels and resolveConceptTypeLabel look them up by BCP-47 tag, trying the full tag, then the primary subtag, then falling back to English, keeping localization deterministic and model-free.

extractMermaidFences returns every fenced ```mermaid block with its line indices, indentation, and backtick marker for round-tripping, and tracks generic fences so a ```mermaid example nested inside a longer fenced block is ignored.

findInvalidMermaidFences validates each fence with the authoritative mermaid.parse when the optional mermaid/jsdom peer dependencies are installed, and otherwise falls back to a conservative heuristicError that flags only near-certain breakages (reserved `end` flowchart node id, semicolon in a label, unescaped angle bracket in a label) so valid diagrams are never degraded.

loadMermaid imports mermaid lazily and memoized, always calls ensureDomGlobals first, and resolves to undefined (falling back to heuristics rather than crashing) when the optional peer dependencies are missing or the load fails.

ensureDomGlobals installs a jsdom window and document because Mermaid's flowchart and state-diagram parsers call DOMPurify which requires a DOM; ordering requires the globals to exist before mermaid is first imported, so mermaid must be loaded only through loadMermaid and never imported directly elsewhere.

degradeInvalidMermaidFences rewrites a document bottom-up, replacing each invalid ```mermaid fence with a ```text fence preserving the body and preceded by an HTML comment (beginning `openwiki: mermaid parse failed`) that embeds the parser error so a later run can repair it, returning the input unchanged when every fence parses.

sanitizeMermaidError makes a parser error safe to embed in an HTML comment by redacting secrets via sanitizeDiagnosticText, flattening to one line while keeping the `Expecting ... got ...` diagnosis, collapsing the comment-terminating `--` sequence, and length-capping the result.

validateWikiMermaid walks the generated wiki through the backend virtual filesystem (rooted at `/` for local-wiki output and `/openwiki` for code output), scans non-reserved Markdown files, degrades invalid fences in place, leaves files with no failing fences byte-for-byte unchanged, and returns counts of files scanned, fences checked, fences degraded, and repaired files.

The OKF output passes run in a fixed finalizer order: preparation migrates pages to OKF and snapshots provenance, then finalization validates Mermaid, synchronizes indexes, validates internal links, synchronizes claim sources, and finalizes generated provenance.

migrateWikiToOkf (pre-run) normalizes every concept page's frontmatter in place without touching indexes, while synchronizeWikiIndexes (post-authoring) re-normalizes each concept file it visits and renders directory indexes; both share the same normalizeConceptFile/normalizeConceptContent repair path so a page is normalized at least once per run regardless of which pass reaches it first.

synchronizeWikiIndexes returns a report-only WikiFrontmatterReport with generatedPages (pages still carrying openwiki_generated: true, i.e. code-derived type/title) and missingDescriptionPages (pages indexed without a usable description); the signals describe metadata quality the pass leaves as-is, do not affect validateOkfFrontmatter or the OKF repair it feeds, and never fail the run.

openwiki/.run.json is a schemaVersion:1 RepositoryRunState checkpoint (runId, mode, phase planning/generating, startedAt, language, actor.producerActor/metadataModel, sourceFingerprint, beforeContentSnapshot, preparedWiki) written atomically and validated with a strict Zod schema; its preparedWiki.generatedProvenance carries the pre-authoring body hashes and prior generated events, and the checkpoint is removed only after the run fully completes so begin() can reconstruct and retry on earlier failure.

openwiki/.page-manifest.json is a schemaVersion:1 RepositoryPageManifest ledger mapping canonical page paths to a RepositoryPageManifestEntry (pageVersion SHA-256 of verified Markdown, optional completedBy/completedRunId, gitHead/sourceFingerprint). An entry is built by buildManifestEntry only from mutually consistent durable Markdown and verified Claims state, throwing invalid_state when they disagree, so coverage can never be recorded for an unverified page.

getCurrentRepositoryPageCompletion rechecks the current page hash and Claims verification against the stored manifest entry before accepting durable coverage, so a stale entry cannot promote a pending page job; on a successful whole-run finish replaceRepositoryPageManifest rewrites the ledger for the surviving page set, preserving the exact prior entry for skipped pages and retaining the prior source checkpoint for pages the run never recompleted.

The verified frontmatter family is reconciled by the Claims runtime's synchronizeClaimsVerification: it retains human/process/other producer events, drops only events whose by is in the openwiki/<version> actor family, normalizes a bare verifier mapping to the canonical list form when the field is touched, and writes nothing when the projected set already matches.

The sources frontmatter family is projected by synchronizeClaimSources from page-owned Claims evidence: producer-authored source entries are retained, while OpenWiki-owned entries get deterministic openwiki-source-<digest> IDs derived from their resource so a later reconciliation can replace or remove only its own projection; both projections route through repairOkfFrontmatter so the resulting frontmatter stays valid even when the input was malformed.

Every deterministic OKF wiki operation runs inside the finalizer middleware's telemetry wrapper, tagged at its origin: preparation tasks under inStage("build", { errorClass: "okf_error", errorDetail: operation }) for operation migrate/provenance_snapshot, and finalization under inStage("finalize", { errorClass: "okf_error", errorDetail: operation }) for operation mermaid/index_sync/link_validation/claims_sources/generated_provenance. The stable errorDetail is the same identifier exposed by WikiFinalizerOperation/WikiPreparationOperation, and the first origin tag wins as the error unwinds.

The OKF middleware's wrapToolCall does not throw: it runs the tool, then addFrontmatterWarning deterministically repairs wiki Markdown the agent just wrote via repairPersistedFile, appending a WARNING block (listing each issue [code] and optional line) to the tool message only when the repair cannot be persisted or re-read, so recoverable tool errors stay recoverable rather than becoming fatal run failures.
